      <title>Burial of King Oyo takes place in Uganda as news anchor prepares for throne</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/12/burial-king-oyo-uganda</link>
      <description><p>Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma</p><p>Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/10/uganda-king-secret-son-succession-dispute">a bitter succession battle</a> behind ​it.</p><p>Oyo’s appointed successor, the news anchor Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, cast nine coffee berries into the grave at the Karambi Royal Tombs, marking the formal handover of power in the western Ugandan kingdom.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/12/burial-king-oyo-uganda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/12/nigerians-extradited-online-romance-scams</link>
      <description><p>Alleged members of Black Axe criminal network that swindled US women out of $6m flown from South Africa</p><p>Six Nigerian nationals linked to an organized criminal network that allegedly swindled American women out of more than $6m through <a href="https://apnews.com/article/scams-online-scams-ai-internet-safety-phishing-fraud-takeaways-b1350fd421cce73ac585a649b07332d5">online romance scams</a> were extradited to the United States on Friday.</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/southafrica">South African</a> police confirmed they were to be extradited earlier on Friday, while <a href="https://citizen.digital/article/six-nigerians-extradited-to-us-over-alleged-ksh700m-romance-scams-n390051#google_vignette">local news</a> in Africa confirmed that the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, known as the Hawks, facilitated their handover to officials from the US Federal Bureau of Investigation and Secret Service at Cape Town international airport, in collaboration with Interpol South Africa.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/12/nigerians-extradited-online-romance-scams">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/sep/11/15m-fund-launched-to-create-unstoppable-momentum-to-end-fgm-worldwide</link>
      <description><p>Her Horizon Fund seeks $100m to stop practice harming 230m women and girls globally  </p><p>Frontline activists and leaders in the fight against female genital mutilation, which has affected more than <a href="https://data.unicef.org/topic/child-protection/female-genital-mutilation/">230 million women and girls worldwide</a>, have welcomed an unprecedented $15.5m (£11.4m) fund aimed at creating “unstoppable momentum” to finally end the practice.</p><p>The launch of the fund comes as <a href="https://equalitynow.org/resource/reports/global-backlash-against-womens-and-girls-rights-words-and-deeds-update-2025/">women’s rights are increasingly under attack</a> and donor funding is in sharp decline, particularly for work led by FGM survivors in local communities. It is thought to be the largest single philanthropic contribution to ending the practice of FGM.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/sep/11/15m-fund-launched-to-create-unstoppable-momentum-to-end-fgm-worldwide">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Family of late King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV reject committee’s choice of cousin and TV presenter as new monarch</p><p>A traditional Ugandan kingdom has become engulfed in a bitter succession dispute after the family of a king who recently died rejected the selection of a television news anchor as his successor.</p><p>King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, who became the world’s youngest reigning monarch when he took the throne in the kingdom of Tooro in 1995 at the age of three, died on 27 August in the US, where he was receiving cancer treatment.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/10/uganda-king-secret-son-succession-dispute">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The city’s mayor and Tennessee’s governor threw their support behind the name change last month</p><p>The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/nashville">Nashville</a> airport is to be renamed after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/music/dolly-parton">Dolly Parton</a>, a board of commissioners voted on Friday, in tribute to the Smoky Mountain singer who is estimated to bring $1.8bn each year to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/tennessee">Tennessee</a> through her Dollywood theme park.</p><p>The decision ensures that Parton, who died last month at 80 years old, will be memorialized with her name on an airport, although the renaming process will take time to complete.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/12/nashville-airport-dolly-parton">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Calls for Democrats to be shot go unchallenged at Republican convention</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/12/democrats-republican-midterm-convention</link>
      <description><p>Crowd member repeatedly said some Democrats ‘should be shot’ during Ted Cruz’s speech, without senator responding</p><p>On the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and warn against the dangers of violent rhetoric, a crowd at the party’s irregular midterm convention in Dallas repeatedly called for a sitting Senate candidate to be shot, while the Republican senator at the podium never denounced or even noted the outbursts.</p><p>The outbursts came repeatedly during Ted Cruz’s Thursday night address at the American Airlines center, when he named a Democrat he accused of holding radical views. After the senator mentioned the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, video footage depicts at least one audience member shouting: “He should be shot!” The same cry followed when Cruz named Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and again after he named Texas Senate candidate James Talarico. Cruz did not pause or respond to the shouting, and it remains unclear whether he heard it from the stage. Cruz did not respond to a request for comment.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/12/democrats-republican-midterm-convention">Continue reading...</a></description>
